requirements.text: First launch requires naming the other person before any card can exist; there is no solo-use path anywhere in the app.
Onboarding generates a real, shareable join code/link string, but onboarding copy explicitly states this offline build cannot deliver a real invite to a second device.
"Preview with a sample partner" is reachable from onboarding/Today and fully simulates the second user so every downstream state (waiting, complete, streak, Timeline) is reachable offline.
A distinct, honestly-labeled 'redeem your own join code' affordance (separate from sample-partner preview) exists to simulate a real partner actually joining.
When the redeem-code affordance fires, all sample-partner Cards/streak/Timeline data is discarded (not merged) and the transition to the real Connection is shown as a distinct visible beat.
Both people set a home location via city search over a bundled city seed list; no network/map-tile dependency exists anywhere in location selection.
Home location is stored and displayed at city-level precision only, never GPS-precise or continuously tracked, disclosed plainly in onboarding copy.
The globe is rendered natively in SwiftUI Canvas using an orthographic projection with bundled simplified coastline polylines; no 3rd-party map/3D engine and no network calls.
Distance between the two home locations is computed via the haversine formula and displayed live on Today.
The tether is a great-circle arc between the two points, sampled and clipped to the front hemisphere, stroked in amber with an additive glow.

The tether draw-on (~1.1s trim animation) and endpoint ignite play only on first pairing and on card completion; ordinary app reopens show an instantly state-legible first frame with no animation delay.

Today's first rendered frame truthfully conveys card state (waiting-on-them / waiting-on-you / complete) with zero required taps and before any animation plays, verified by a pure Card→CardDisplayState unit test independent of animation timing.
Today shows a dual clock (both people's local times) and today's shared prompt in its current state.
The Answer sheet is the only free-text entry surface anywhere in the app.
The one-line answer enforces an explicit maximum character cap at the input level, not just visual wrapping.
Submitting an answer fires a crisp `.rigid` tick haptic and moves the card to "waiting for them" or completes it if the partner already answered.
If a SwiftData save fails on answer submission, the Answer sheet retains the typed draft and shows an explicit retry/error state instead of discarding the input.
Once both answers exist, the card is complete and both answers become permanently uneditable; this finality is visibly communicated at the moment of submission.
Card 'today' and streak evaluation are anchored to a canonical UTC day boundary computed at the Connection level, never to either person's local calendar day.

The gated-reveal state machine implements exactly awaitingBoth → awaitingThem/awaitingMe → complete, running against the LocalSyncService protocol with a timer-driven simulated partner (never a hardcoded pre-completed fixture).

Deterministic seeded-fixture tests cover: simultaneous both-answer-same-tick, the simulated partner's timer firing while the app is backgrounded mid-submission, and the simulated partner's timer firing while the Answer sheet is open with an uncommitted draft (state updates without touching/losing the open draft).
A two-beat 'heartbeat' haptic (.soft, ~140ms apart) fires when the simulated partner's answer lands while the app is foregrounded; this is explicitly not required/tested for backgrounded delivery.
A success notification haptic fires on card completion, and the tether visually snaps taut with the crisp tick.
The streak UI shows the user's personal answer streak separately from the connection's shared completion streak.
A broken completion streak legibly attributes whether the break was caused by the user or by their partner not answering.
A missed canonical UTC day resets the completion streak to 0 the following day, and this reset is visibly surfaced in the UI.
After the bundled 60-day prompt list is exhausted, prompts repeat from day 1 with a visible 'you've answered this before' badge.
Every completed card threads into a vertical Timeline; tapping a past card lets the user relive or re-share it.

Compose & Share lets a user pick a skin (only classic indigo is populated; the skin enum is architected as a real extension point), preview, and export a static PNG watermarked with the join link, with no paywall on this base export.

The animated-export toggle is visible and paywall-gated correctly for free users; for an entitled Tether+ user it resolves to an explicit 'coming soon' state rather than crashing, silently no-opping, or producing a fake file.
The paywall is presented at exactly three triggers: tapping animated export, tapping 'add a connection', and opening Reunion — and is honest about what is/isn't gated.
The Reunion screen is reachable from the app and correctly fires the paywall for a free (non-Tether+) user.
Connections & Settings is a single flat list containing: notification cadence, units (km/mi), subscription status, and sign-out — no sub-screens.
The notification-cadence control's copy is explicitly scoped to in-app/foreground alerts only, or is disabled with an honest explanation — it never implies working push notifications.
An entitled (Tether+) user can create a second Connection via a bare 'add connection' action; a free user attempting this is blocked and routed to the paywall.
'Primary connection' is deterministically the earliest-created Connection; any additional connection created after it becomes read-only (never deleted) if Tether+ lapses.

A StoreKit-Testing-simulated expired/lapsed subscription test exercises the downgrade path end-to-end: create a second connection while entitled, simulate expiration, assert the primary stays fully editable and the second becomes read-only with zero data deleted.
StoreKit 2 purchases (monthly $4.99, yearly $29.99, 7-day trial) succeed in the Simulator against a bundled .storekit configuration.
All colors and fonts are defined only in DesignSystem.swift; an automated lint script fails the build if inline Color()/UIColor()/.font(.system(size:)) appear anywhere else.
Amber appears only on the tether arc, the two glowing endpoints, and the single primary 'light the tether' action — nowhere else in the UI, verified by the lint gate.

CoreMotion-driven globe parallax degrades gracefully to a static neutral angle with no crash when CMDeviceMotion is unavailable (the Simulator default), verified by a unit test constructing the parallax provider with no motion manager.
With Reduce Motion enabled, the globe shows a static view with cross-fade instead of the draw-on trim animation, while haptics still fire; verified by a unit test toggling the accessibility flag.
The hand-drawn Canvas globe exposes an explicit VoiceOver accessibility label/value summarizing distance and card state (e.g. 'You are 2,847 km from [name]. Card complete.').
Every reachable screen supports full dark mode via semantic color roles and scales with Dynamic Type via relativeTo: text styles.
Every reachable screen defines and shows explicit empty, loading, success, and error states where that screen can reach those states (no bare blank views or placeholder text).

All eight named screens (Onboarding/Pair, Today, Answer sheet, Compose & Share, Timeline, Reunion, Connections & Settings, Paywall) are fully reachable and populated with no placeholders via the sample-partner and/or redeem-code paths, entirely offline.
No screen beyond these eight named screens is built.
Globe rendering stays within a fixed coastline-vertex budget and throttles parallax updates rather than applying every raw CoreMotion callback, to avoid stutter under active parallax.
For an entitled (Tether+) user, Reunion additionally supports setting a target date and shows a real countdown with its own hero visual.

Animated MP4/Live Photo export, the three additional premium skins, the Year Tethered retrospective reel, real invite networking, localization, WidgetKit/watchOS targets, and anti-clock-tampering defenses are explicitly not built in this iteration.
